result.text: CP-CML MCyR 54% (144/267) overall (49% resistant, 70% T315I); AP-CML MaHR 52% (43/83) overall (55% resistant, 39% T315I); BP-CML MaHR 31% (19/62); Ph+ALL MaHR 41% (13/32).

citations.quote:
- The primary endpoint for patients with CP-CML was Major Cytogenetic Response (MCyR). The MCyR rate was 54% (144/267) overall in patients with CP-CML; 49% (99/203) in the resistant cohort and 70% (45/64) in the T315I cohort.
- The primary endpoint for patients with AP-CML was Major Hematologic Response (MaHR). The MaHR rate was 52% (43/83) overall in patients with AP-CML; 55% (36/65) in the resistant cohort and 39% (7/18) in the T315I cohort.
- The primary endpoint for patients with BP-CML or Ph+ALL was also MaHR. The MaHR rate was 31% (19/62) in patients with BP-CML and 41% (13/32) in patients with Ph+ ALL.

Hematologic adverse reactions included thrombocytopenia, anemia, neutropenia, lymphopenia, and leukopenia (6).

Serious bleeding events, occurred in 5% (22/449) of patients treated with Iclusig, including fatalities.

detail.text: WARNING: ARTERIAL THROMBOSIS and HEPATOTOXICITY. Serious arterial thrombosis (cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, peripheral vascular), including fatal MI and stroke, occurred in 8% of patients; hepatotoxicity, liver failure, and death have occurred.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: ARTERIAL THROMBOSIS and HEPATOTOXICITY

- Cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and peripheral vascular thrombosis, including fatal myocardial infarction and stroke have occurred in Iclusig-treated patients. In clinical trials, serious arterial thrombosis occurred in 8% of Iclusig-treated patients. Interrupt and consider discontinuation of Iclusig in patients who develop arterial thrombotic events (2.3) (5.1).

- Hepatotoxicity, liver failure and death have occurred in Iclusig-treated patients. Monitor hepatic function prior to and during treatment. Interrupt and then reduce or discontinue Iclusig for hepatotoxicity (2.3) (5.2).
